title: More Methods
story: You're designing a floor-planning tool. Users draw rectangles, and you need to instantly calculate the area and perimeter — because nobody wants to multiply width by height manually!
why: Methods that compute values from fields make your structs self-sufficient — ask a rectangle for its area instead of calculating it yourself.
analogy: Methods on a Rectangle are like asking a room questions — "What's your floor area?" or "How much baseboard do you need?" — the room knows the answer.
try_it: Add an `is_tall` method that returns true if the height is greater than the width. Test it with a tall rectangle and a wide rectangle.
tips: Methods that compute something should return a value — don't just print inside the method
Name methods that return Bool like questions: `is_square`, `is_wide`, `can_fit`
Use `2.0` not `2` when multiplying Float64 values to keep the type consistent
common_mistakes: Accidentally writing `2 * (width + height)` instead of `2.0 * (...)` — mixing Int and Float64 gives a type error
Forgetting the return type annotation — `fn Rectangle.area(self) -> Float64` needs the `-> Float64`
Printing inside the method instead of returning the value — let the caller decide what to do with the result
